name: Guardian genius crossword No 187
preamble: Five clues contain a cryptically superfluous word. Wordplay in 14 other clues contains a cryptically superfluous letter. Unclued entries are five pairs of characters linked cryptically to each other and to one of the five superfluous words. The superfluous letters in clue order give two further characters and a third word linked in the same way. Eleven of the characters are (or were) real people; one isn’t.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: One hearing Dralon curtains last getting more in

indicators.note: curtains enclose a window, so one piece is drawn around the other here

blocks.note: a trier is one who hears and judges a case in court
the last part of something is its end
superfluous word, ignored in the wordplay; Dralon is a velvety upholstery fabric

explanation.surface: Someone listening to a case is distracted by Dralon curtains, a fabric that once seemed the height of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: TR(END)IER. Dralon is a superfluous word: its letters rearrange to ARNOLD and ROLAND, tying it to the unclued pair MATTHEW (Arnold) and (Roland) RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In' as an adjective means fashionable, so 'more in' is its comparative, a synonym for more stylish.

clue.text: Writer in front upset about book review

indicators.note: to review something is to go over it again, here reworking these letters
about means surrounding, so the word for front goes round the other piece
in a down clue, upset turns the whole piece upside down, reading it from the bottom

blocks.note: the van is the front of an army or procession, as in vanguard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer at the front of a newspaper is upset about a review of his book.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Nun and cashier breaking cover

indicators.note: breaking smashes the words apart so their letters can be reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; its H is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: A nun and a bank teller break cover, like fugitives emerging from hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: The H of CASHIER, this clue's superfluous letter, is left out of the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is protection against loss, and the policy is called cover, as in 'fully covered'.

clue.text: Left relax with socialist publication

blocks.note: red is a common term for a socialist or communist
L is the abbreviation for left
to ease off is to relax

explanation.surface: A left-winger unwinding with a socialist magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The D of RED is this clue's superfluous letter. 'With' simply joins the pieces, which are not in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A release is something issued for the public, such as a press release, film or record, so a publication.

clue.text: Underground room to call mine

blocks.note: to cry out is to call
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Calling a cellar a mine, as if it were dug out of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of PIT is this clue's superfluous letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is a vault or chamber beneath a church, so a room below ground level.

clue.text: Song taken up in revels disowning the Queen and her supporters

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, from the bottom
disowning casts something off, so those letters are removed
in says the turned song sits inside the other word

blocks.note: a lay is a ballad or song
to roister is to revel noisily
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Monarchists sing a song at a party that has turned against the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' refers back to the Queen, so the definition borrows the wordplay's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalists support the monarchy, and so are the supporters of the reigning Queen.

clue.text: Fat fellow at work? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word for work survives, the rest dropped

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
labour is hard work

explanation.surface: A sneer at an overweight colleague on the job, softened with the British 'not half', meaning very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'absolutely'; here it literally keeps half of LABOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Flab is loose excess body fat, so the noun fat is a direct synonym.

clue.text: In Torbay selling fish

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words, from the R of the first to the S of the second, signalled by 'In'

explanation.surface: A fishmonger trading on the seafront at Torbay, a resort bay in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run is RBAYS; its B is one of the fourteen superfluous letters and drops out to leave RAYS. Those letters in clue order spell BILL SMITH DIODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are flat cartilaginous sea fish related to sharks, such as skates and stingrays.

clue.text: Sect member increasingly unsteady

blocks.note: more unsteady is shakier, the comparative of shaky

explanation.surface: A member of a religious group seems to be wobbling more and more.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of SHAKIER is the superfluous letter for this clue, so it drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakers are an American Christian sect famed for ecstatic dancing in worship and plain furniture.

clue.text: Behave with spirit in a positive manner

blocks.note: to act is to behave
doing something with spirit is doing it in a lively way

explanation.surface: Advice to conduct yourself energetically and with a can-do attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of LIVELY is this clue's superfluous letter and is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something actively is to engage with it purposefully rather than passively, a positive, energetic way of acting.

clue.text: Idiot girl

blocks.note: lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a girl

explanation.surface: A rude two-word insult aimed at a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of LASS is this clue's superfluous letter, leaving ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish, stupid person, a common informal synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Rock plant by lake pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means drawn upwards, so read from the bottom

blocks.note: Bala is a lake in north Wales
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A rock-garden plant growing by a lake has been uprooted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock plant' looks like one phrase, an alpine; it splits into definition and wordplay. Bala Lake (Llyn Tegid) is the largest natural lake in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine translucent white mineral, a form of gypsum, carved into ornaments, so a kind of rock.

clue.text: One over from Forest of Arden wasted shots

indicators.note: from here means taken away from what follows, so a letter is removed
something wasted is ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over; only one of the two in the fodder goes
taken as written
superfluous word, ignored in the wordplay; the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A hunter misses his targets in Shakespeare's Forest of Arden.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden is a superfluous word: it rearranges to NADER and ANDRE, linking the unclued RALPH (Nader) and (Andre) AGASSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts can mean attempts, and a shot is an attempt at something, as in 'have a shot'.

clue.text: Like some twins for a threesome initially? Run during way over

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
during means within, so the letter sits inside the word for way
over means turned over, so the piece is read the other way

blocks.note: taken as written; its O is the superfluous letter
taken as written
the opening letter of the word
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a lane is a narrow way or road

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about which twins might be up for a threesome, followed by advice to run.
explanation.walkthrough: The O of FOR is this clue's superfluous letter. The blogger at fifteensquared doubted the clue's soundness, since 'initially' can be read as applying to all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraternal twins develop from two separate eggs, unlike identical twins, so only some twins are described this way.

clue.text: Around room forcibly assert support for chair

indicators.note: doing something forcibly suggests violent disruption, so the letters are rearranged
around says the shuffled word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: RM is the standard abbreviation for room
taken as written; one of its S letters is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to state your case forcefully, oddly mixed with a room and a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two S letters in the fodder is this clue's superfluous letter, so only five letters are rearranged. 'Chair' is the furniture, not a person chairing a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is the part of a chair that supports the sitter's arm, so it is a support for a chair.

clue.text: Struggled — time for women's support

indicators.note: x for y means x takes the place of y in the word

blocks.note: to wrestle is to struggle
T is the abbreviation for time
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A struggle ends with the declaration that the time has come for women's support.
explanation.walkthrough: T replaces W, and the D of WRESTLED is the superfluous letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of a beam on splayed legs that holds up a table top, so a support.

clue.text: Country people safe? Hang about!

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so these letters are turned round into new order

blocks.note: taken as written; its E is the superfluous letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Villagers asking whether they are safe, told to wait a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's country people are rustics; the definition means the people of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghans are the people of Afghanistan, so they are a country's people, its citizens.

clue.text: Some slip close to the flower garden

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: some of something is part of it
to slip is to make a mistake, to err
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing near the flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal ornamental garden with flower beds laid out in a symmetrical pattern.

clue.text: Egyptian god carrying round ankh with new tree

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the god holds the next pieces

blocks.note: Ra was the Egyptian sun god
O is round in shape
W is the abbreviation for with
N is the abbreviation for new
superfluous word, ignored in the wordplay; the ankh is the Egyptian hieroglyph for life

explanation.surface: An Egyptian god holding a round ankh beside a young tree, like a temple carving.
explanation.walkthrough: Ankh is a superfluous word: it rearranges to KHAN and HANK, linking the unclued AMIR (Khan) and (Hank) MARVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan or mountain ash is a small tree with clusters of red berries.

clue.text: Report I filed in issue over drug

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, so the word is read upwards
in places the letter inside the turned word

blocks.note: taken as written
a son is issue, meaning offspring
E is short for ecstasy, the drug
superfluous word, ignored in the wordplay

explanation.surface: A journalist filed a story about a drug problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Filed is a superfluous word: it rearranges to FIELD and FIDEL, linking the unclued SALLY (Field) and (Fidel) CASTRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, such as a gunshot, so it is a kind of noise.

clue.text: Get off with female and make an impression — niello!

indicators.note: off with means cut away, so a letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: to fetch something is to go and get it
F is the standard abbreviation for female
superfluous word, ignored in the wordplay; niello is a black inlay used in engraved metalwork

explanation.surface: A cheeky pick-up line and an artist's exclamation about decorative metalwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Niello is a superfluous word: it rearranges to O'NEILL and LIONEL, linking the unclued EUGENE (O'Neill) and (Lionel) SHRIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design by cutting or corroding a surface, literally making an impression in it.

clue.text: God's female, feminist ultimately claimed

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word it follows
something claimed is taken in and held, so the word for female holds the letter

blocks.note: a woman is a female person
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A feminist has finally laid claim to a goddess, the female side of the divine.
explanation.walkthrough: WOMAN takes in T, and its M, the superfluous letter here, drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: Wotan is the chief god in Germanic mythology and in Wagner's Ring cycle, the counterpart of the Norse Odin.

clue.text: Make use of? In a word, wrong!

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters must be put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; its I is the superfluous letter

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a scheme's use in a single damning word: wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I, this clue's superfluous letter, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on resources is to use them, to make use of them as a source to rely on.

clue.text: Was inclined to go after number engaged

indicators.note: to go after means to follow, so one piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: ten is a number
a ship that listed leaned over to one side

explanation.surface: Someone felt disposed to follow a number of people who had signed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of TEN is this clue's superfluous letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to engage or sign up for military service, so enlisted and engaged are synonyms in that sense.
